ERCOT.basis: Texas is building a roughly $33B high-voltage grid for oil-field and data-center demand, shared by all ERCOT customers. Little is in rates yet; the range shows its data-center share once built.
ERCOT.label: Texas (ERCOT)

CAISO.basis: Little is in rates yet. Over $2B of new South Bay power lines for data centers will be shared by all California grid customers as they come online; PG&E says big new loads can lower rates.
CAISO.label: California (CAISO)

MISO.basis: Midwest capacity prices jumped about tenfold in 2025, partly on data-center demand, but most utilities here own their plants, so little reaches home bills directly.
MISO.label: the Midwest grid (MISO)

SPP.basis: Kansas and Missouri approved large-load rates in 2025 designed to make data centers cover their own costs instead of households.
SPP.label: the Southwest Power Pool

ISO-NE.basis: New England's grid operator says data centers are not yet a major driver of demand; only a few hundred megawatts are in study.
ISO-NE.label: New England

NYISO.basis: Few large data centers are connected in New York yet, so the effect on today's bills is near zero.
NYISO.label: New York

Southeast.basis: Georgia approved a big data-center power build-out in Dec 2025 on condition it not add a projected $20/month to home bills through 2031. Other Southern utilities haven't published a figure.
Southeast.label: the Southeast

West.basis: Arizona's APS has proposed raising data-center rates about 45% versus about 14% for homes so households don't subsidize them; the case is still pending.
West.label: the West
